originality.rationale: The established degree-two congruence is already stated for the normalized sequence, so the claim deliberately excludes it as the principal novelty. The general simultaneous coefficients 0<=r<p, explicit affine prime-step law for every shift, and sharp cutoff are not implied by the individually stated polynomial definitions, fixed-diagonal congruences, or the inspected 2015 de Bruijn graph enumerative results. Targeted public research-index and primary-literature comparisons did not reveal an equivalent statement; completeness of prior art is not guaranteed.
residual_risks: A 1946 original primary scan was not fully inspected; no priority conclusion is drawn from unread pages.
A later or older general theorem for factorial-binomial rook transforms could imply the uniform affine classification despite the targeted negative searches.
The degree-two statement is already present in OEIS A000426 and is treated only as a corollary, not independently novel.

value.rationale: Ménage hit polynomials encode a historically central rook-permutation problem; their prime-step simultaneous low-degree arithmetic behavior is natural and not determined by a single OEIS diagonal. The uniform all-prime/all-shift affine formula gives complete residue evolution for an entire truncated polynomial, with an intrinsic sharp cutoff and explicit effective computation. The result is motivated by a documented prime congruence question and has structural content beyond routine finite tabulation.
